lesson_title: Seven Questions, Full Marks: The Physics Practice Run
hook_text: The Doppler question has exactly one decision in it — a plus or a minus — and it is worth the whole answer.
clip_script: The only decision is the sign in the denominator, and the reasoning that never fails: approach must raise the frequency, so the denominator must shrink — subtract the source speed; recession must lower it — add the source speed. Approaching: observed frequency equals 340 over, 340 minus 20, times 900, which is 340 over 320 times 900. That is 306 000 over 320 — 956,25 hertz. Higher than 900, as approach demands.
visual_style: A train sweeping past a listener on a platform, sound waves bunching ahead and stretching behind, with the Doppler fraction assembling on screen and the denominator sign flashing as the single decision point.
mood: One-decision tension — the entire question balancing on a plus or a minus.
pacing: Slow zoom onto the denominator, the sign snapping into place, then the numbers cascading to 956,25 hertz.
call_to_action: Walk all seven physics questions at examination pace in the full practice run.
